description.summary: what neue-comp and neue-shell tell each other

protocol.description:
A private neueOS protocol (docs/protocols/neue-shell-v1.md, ADR 0066) between the compositor and the shell (menu bar, dock, OSDs). The compositor tells the shell about the windows and which one is active, and routes the system keys (volume, brightness, media) to it; the shell asks the compositor to activate, minimise and close windows, to run compositor actions and to send key chords to the active window.
Privileged: the global is only offered to the shell, the client the compositor spawned on a private connection. No other client sees it, and binding it anyway is a protocol error.

interface.name: neue_shell_manager_v1

description.summary: the shell's view of the compositor

interface.description: On bind, the compositor sends a toplevel event for every window that is mapped or minimised, each followed by that toplevel's state and done, then one active event. After that it sends toplevel for each new window and active whenever the active window changes.

enum.name: system_key

description.summary: keys the compositor hands to the shell

enum.description: A version of this interface sends only the keys it lists.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Toplevel objects made through this manager keep existing but get no more events; the client should destroy them too.

request.name: run_action
request.description: Run the action called name, as `neuectl action` does (`neuectl actions` lists them). toplevel is the window it acts on; null means the active window, or none for actions that take no window. Actions that need further arguments (move-window, resize-window) fail. The result object reports the outcome once.

request.name: send_shortcut

description.summary: press a key chord in the active window

request.description: Press the modifiers, then the key that produces keysym in the current keyboard layout, then release them in reverse order, as if typed. The keys go to the active window, which is given the keyboard first if something else (a shell menu) has it. This is how the fallback Edit menu runs Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All. Ignored when no window is active, when the layout has no key for keysym, or while the session is locked.

arg.name: keysym
arg.summary: an XKB keysym, e.g. 0x63 for c

event.name: toplevel
event.description: A window was mapped, or existed when the manager was bound. Its state follows, ending with done.

event.name: active
event.description: The window whose app owns the menu bar: the one with keyboard focus, or, while a layer surface (a shell menu), a popup or the lock screen has the keyboard, the window that had it before. Null when no window is active (the desktop was clicked, the last window closed or was minimised). Sent after the toplevel's own events, so its state is known.

event.name: system_key

description.summary: a system key was pressed or released

event.description: The volume, brightness and media keys go to the shell instead of the focused client, also while the session is locked or a client inhibits shortcuts. A compositor key binding for the same key wins. Repeat is up to the shell (it knows the rate from wl_keyboard.repeat_info). modifiers are the ones held.

interface.name: neue_shell_toplevel_v1

description.summary: one window, as the shell sees it

interface.description: State events are buffered and applied together on done. The first batch always carries identifier, title, app_id, state, icon and one of the menu events; later batches carry only what changed (an icon change sends icon and its icon_buffer events again).

entry.name: attention
entry.summary: it asked for focus it was not given (the dock bounces)

request.name: destroy
request.description: Sent after closed, or when the shell no longer cares. The window is unaffected.

request.name: activate
request.description: Restores it first if it is minimised.

description.summary: minimise the window and its dialogs
restore and focus a minimised window

request.name: close
request.description: The app may refuse or ask to save first.

request.name: set_minimize_rectangle
request.description: The rectangle, in the surface's coordinates, that the window's minimise and restore animation runs towards: the dock tile of its app. The surface must be one of the shell's layer surfaces. A width or height of 0 unsets it. The rectangle follows the surface when it moves.

event.name: identifier
event.description: Sent once, first. `window-N`, where N is the window's `neuectl` id; the same string as the window's ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier.

event.name: icon
event.description: Replaces the icon. name is the icon theme name the app set, or null; the icon_buffer events that follow before done are its images. Null with no buffers: the app set no icon, and the shell uses the one for its app id.

event.name: icon_buffer
event.description: A read-only, sealed memfd holding width × height pixels in ARGB8888 (premultiplied alpha, little-endian, as wl_shm), rows of width × 4 bytes with no padding. scale is the buffer scale the app gave it.

event.name: menu_dbusmenu
event.description: The window exports com.canonical.dbusmenu at service and path (from the KDE appmenu protocol). The strings passed a syntax check only (ADR 0025).

event.name: menu_gmenu
event.description: The window exports its menus with GMenu at bus_name (from gtk_shell1). Paths the app did not give are null. The strings passed a syntax check only.

description.summary: no exported menus: the shell shows the fallback menu
apply the state events sent since the last done

event.name: closed
event.description: No more events follow. The client should destroy the object.

interface.name: neue_shell_action_v1
interface.description: Exactly one of its events is sent, and then the object is gone.

event.name: failed
event.description: message says why (an unknown action, a missing window, a missing argument).
